title: Kitchener Central Transit Hub approvals and speed cameras
subtitle: Petersburg water charges, Duke Street road transfer, school-zone speed camera by-law changes, loading zones and a Cambridge tax grant assignment.
overview: The committee advanced several items tied to the Kitchener Central Transit Hub. It recommended selling a narrow strip of surplus Regional land to Metrolinx for $1,434,000 {{vote:m4}}, approving the preferred design for Victoria Street North {{vote:m5}}, and starting the process to take over part of Duke Street West from the City of Kitchener {{vote:m6}}. Staff said these steps allow detailed design and a rail underpass to proceed, with construction work expected from 2025.

The committee also recommended by-law changes for the municipal speed camera program, effective January 1, 2025 {{vote:m8}}. This adds school zones, speed reductions and community safety zones across several municipalities. Some councillors raised concerns about 24-hour enforcement and short 40 km/h sections on rural roads.

It also recommended a by-law to recover the cost of Petersburg water system upgrades from benefiting properties {{vote:m7}}. Smaller items on the consent agenda were approved, including new loading zones on Duke Street and Weber Street in Kitchener. Because this is a standing committee, these recommendations go to Regional Council for final decisions.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended declaring Regional lands near Victoria Street North in Kitchener surplus and selling them to Metrolinx for $1,434,000.

The committee recommended approving the preferred preliminary design between Weber Street West and King Street West and filing the Notice of Completion for the environmental assessment, with a 30-day public record period.
The committee recommended starting the process to transfer Duke Street West, between the CN tracks and Breithaupt Street, from the City of Kitchener to the Region.
The committee recommended enacting a by-law charging benefiting Petersburg landowners for the cost of upgrades to the water system the Region assumed.
The committee recommended amending the Traffic and Parking By-law, effective January 1, 2025, to support the municipal speed camera program.

decisions.item: 49 Queen Street East tax increment grant
decisions.detail: The committee recommended assigning the Brownfield tax increment grant and redevelopment agreement for 49 Queen Street East, Cambridge, to the property's new owner.

decisions.item: Duke and Weber Street loading zones
decisions.detail: The committee recommended amending the Traffic and Parking By-law to adjust limited parking and loading zones on Duke Street and the school bus loading zone on Weber Street East in Kitchener.

debate: On the hub, one councillor said the 66 planned parking spaces seemed light, citing past parking assumptions for the LRT that fell through. Staff said the final number is not set, a pick-up and drop-off area is being added, and more parking is expected at a future Breslau GO station.

On selling the surplus lands, one councillor asked about keeping public land in public hands. Staff said the land is a narrow sliver beside the rail corridor that has no practical other use. Staff added that the sale proceeds go to general funds and effectively offset the Victoria Street project cost.

On speed cameras, councillors worried that short 40 km/h stretches between 60 km/h transition zones on rural roads would frustrate drivers. Staff said best practice is a transition of about 500 metres, and the plan includes 90 days' notice before cameras start.

Another councillor objected to 24-hour, year-round enforcement and said drivers would see it as a cash grab. Others said the program is about safety and that speeders pay for it, and a lower speed greatly improves survival in a crash.

On the Petersburg by-law, a councillor asked what building a new communal system would cost. Staff gave no figure, noting it would require permits, treatment and distribution, and said they would circulate cost information.
